I've spent the past couple of months moving across the country: packing up one house, staying with friends for a couple of weeks, unpacking and painting and fixing up the new house (See all those boxes behind me? They're still packed, because we're replacing that carpet with hardwoods in the next couple of weeks). It's a lot colder here, like winter already, and I need some warm, thicker skirts. I made a trek to Jo Ann's and got a bunch of corduroys, wool, and heavier fabrics (and also some lighter fabrics for blouses to layer under sweaters). Yesterday I got to sew my first project in my new sewing room! My fabric-cutting table hasn't been assembled yet, so I had to cut the fabric on top of my cutting mats on the floor. I couldn't find my pattern weights, so I used cans of food to hold down the paper. I couldn't find my pins either, so I just carefully held everything together when I sewed. Of course as soon as I was done and putting stuff away, I found the box with the weights and pins... But it got done! And I got to wear it last night for my singing event.

I used New Look pattern 6516 view A. I made size 10 (25" waist and 34 1/2" hips). I used a thick chambray fabric.

This pattern was super quick and easy. I used 1" non-roll elastic for the waist (the pattern suggested 1/2"). I am not a fan of elastic waistbands, but I don't mind them if they are a wider elastic. I like to wear belts over the waists anyway (although I couldn't find my wide, dusty pink belt, so I had to wear this grey sash). I also changed the pattern by sewing both of the side seams of the lower part of the skirt. I left the length as it was printed, and that ended up being a perfect skirt length for my 5'9" height.

I recommend the pattern, especially for beginners. I will probably use the same pattern again next summer and make the three-tiered skirt in a cotton or rayon--I think that would be nice.
